headline: Highest risk is medium: Firecrawl can ingest web content and API keys while Plano is a broad-egress gateway, creating plausible prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance pathways in default docs-only setups.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API surfaces, while Plano is an OpenAI-compatible gateway with broad egress. If Firecrawl output is forwarded into Plano as trusted text, attacker-controlled page content can steer downstream prompts. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into Plano prompts or routing context without sanitization
IF both agents share a message queue, clipboard, or MCP bridge without provenance tags
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all Firecrawl-derived text before passing it onward
Disable automatic prompt forwarding between the agents
Require a human review step for any web-derived instructions
Strip HTML/markdown control tokens before ingestion
requires-engineering: implement source-tracking metadata across the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys, screenshots, and structured data, and Plano has broad network egress plus log/trace/metric handling. In a shared workspace or shared principal setup, sensitive Firecrawl inputs can flow into Plano logs or outbound requests. The profiles do not show isolation, so leakage is plausible even though direct exfiltration is not proven.
conditions: IF Firecrawl and Plano run under the same filesystem or OAuth principal
IF Plano logs or forwards request bodies containing Firecrawl inputs
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace before handoff
Turn off verbose logging for Plano during paired runs
Use separate service accounts for each agent
Redact screenshots and API keys before transfer
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate sandboxes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Firecrawl supports multiple instances while Plano does not. That creates overlap on mutable external resources and potential contention if they target the same APIs or shared state. There is no evidence of locking or coordination, so conflicts are plausible though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API, datastore, or queue
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access to shared mutable resources
mitigations: Assign disjoint API credentials to each agent
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Limit one agent to read-only access where possible
Add retry/backoff on write conflicts
requires-engineering: add explicit locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped web content and structured data, while Plano is positioned as a gateway that may route or transform downstream requests. If Plano treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into later actions. The profiles do not document verification gates, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Plano consumes Firecrawl output without an explicit verification step
IF downstream systems act on Plano-transformed content as if it were validated
mitigations: Require citation or source links for every Firecrawl-derived claim
Insert a validation step before Plano forwards content
Mark scraped content as untrusted in prompts
Compare outputs against a second source for critical tasks
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or policy gates

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys, screenshots, and web content, while Plano handles logs, traces, and metrics with broad egress. If regulated or personal data is routed from Firecrawl into Plano telemetry or outbound requests, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No certifications or DPA details are documented here, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data from Firecrawl is included in Plano logs, traces, or metrics
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls that are not configured
mitigations: Exclude secrets and personal data from logs
Set short retention on Plano telemetry
Document the data flow between the agents
Use region-locked endpoints where available
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
